skill.name: godot-gdscript-patterns
skill.description: Develop Godot 4 games with practical GDScript patterns for scenes, signals, resources, state machines, save systems, and performance.
skill.summary: Apply reusable Godot 4 GDScript patterns for maintainable game systems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed one high severity documentation risk: the save system example hard-codes a placeholder encryption key in resources/implementation-playbook.md line 669. The remaining static findings are false positives from Godot local resource loading, regular GDScript comments, node path usage, and Markdown inline code. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Hard-coded encryption key in save system example
remediation.suggestion: Replace the placeholder constant with guidance to derive or load a per-project key outside source control, and warn users not to ship hard-coded keys.

static_findings.snippet: # Create runtime copy to avoid modifying the resource
- **Use signals for decoupling** - Avoid direct references
- **Pool frequently spawned objects** - Avoid GC hitches
- If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(path) loads local Godot resources asynchronously, not an HTTP client or external network request. The surrounding code swaps scenes from project resources.
Line 669 defines a hard-coded encryption key placeholder in a save manager example. Copying this pattern into production would expose encrypted save data to a shared static key.
The line is a comment about duplicating a Godot resource at runtime to avoid mutating source data. It does not inspect the host system or gather environment details.
str(get_path()) stores the node path inside the Godot scene tree as a save identifier. This is not a host filesystem path or system reconnaissance behavior.
The line is a performance comment about avoiding allocations in hot paths. It contains no reconnaissance logic or instruction to inspect the system.
The line is a best practice note about using signals to decouple Godot scenes. It does not request system data or perform reconnaissance.
The line recommends object pooling to reduce garbage collection pauses in games. It is unrelated to host inspection or reconnaissance.
The backticks are Markdown inline formatting around a documentation file path. There is no Ruby code, shell invocation, or command execution.
The backticks are Markdown inline formatting around a resource file path. The skill only tells the agent where examples are documented.

content.value_statement: Godot projects can become hard to maintain when gameplay logic spreads across scenes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable GDScript patterns for cleaner game systems.
actual_capabilities: Explains Godot 4 architecture concepts such as nodes, scenes, signals, resources, and autoloads.
Provides patterns for state machines, components, object pooling, scene management, and save systems.
Guides refactoring toward typed GDScript, signal-based communication, and resource-based data.
Offers performance tips for cached node references, reduced allocations, and process control.
Provides checklists and verification steps for applying patterns inside a Godot project.
limitations: It does not run the Godot editor or execute project tests.
Examples require adaptation for each project structure and gameplay design.
It focuses on Godot 4 and may need changes for Godot 3.
Security-sensitive examples, especially save encryption, need production review.

use_cases.title: Structure a New Gameplay System
use_cases.description: Plan scene responsibilities, signals, and resource data before adding player, enemy, or item logic.

use_cases.title: Refactor Hard-Coupled Scenes
use_cases.description: Convert direct node references into signals, components, and reusable scene patterns.

use_cases.title: Teach Practical GDScript Architecture
use_cases.description: Use the playbook to explain maintainable Godot patterns with focused examples and review prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple State Machine
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Godot GDScript Patterns skill to design a simple player state machine for idle, run, jump, and fall. Include scene setup and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Scene Communication
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Godot scene communication plan and suggest how to replace tight node references with signals, components, or an event bus.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Save System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Godot 4 save system for player progress and level objects. Include safer guidance for save identifiers and encryption key handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Architecture and Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my Godot architecture for state management, object pooling, resources, autoloads, and hot path performance. Return risks, fixes, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable health system for players and enemies.
output: Recommends a HealthComponent node with typed exported values and clear ownership boundaries.
Uses signals for damaged, healed, and died events so scenes stay decoupled.
Adds checks for editor setup, damage flow, and death handling.

output_examples.input: My bullets create frame drops during combat.
output: Suggests object pooling for frequently spawned projectiles.
Calls out setup steps for reusable instances, active state changes, and cleanup.
Adds profiler checks to confirm reduced allocation spikes.

output_examples.input: I want a save system for level objects.
output: Defines saveable node responsibilities and stable identifiers.
Separates global save management from per-object save data.
Warns against shipping a hard-coded encryption key.

best_practices: Use signals for scene communication when systems should remain decoupled.
Keep resources focused on data and place runtime behavior in nodes or components.
Validate every generated pattern inside the target Godot version and project structure.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder encryption keys into production save code.
Do not use autoload singletons for every shared system.
Do not optimize before profiling the actual frame time problem.

faq.question: Does this skill run Godot or test my project?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, patterns, and review prompts. You must run Godot tests and playtests yourself.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Godot 4?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Godot 4 GDScript patterns. Godot 3 projects may require API changes.

faq.question: Can it help with complete gameplay systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan systems such as state machines, components, object pools, scene managers, and save flows.

faq.question: Does it cover multiplayer networking?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The skill focuses on local architecture patterns, not multiplayer protocols or server design.

faq.question: How should I use the save encryption example?
faq.answer: Treat it as a pattern sketch. Replace placeholder keys with secure project-specific key handling before release.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
